children: Sunil D’Souza will assume the chairmanship on November 12, while Jayant Balan is set to take over as managing director in May 2027

Voltas has named Sunil D’Souza as its next chairman, with the leadership change set to take effect on November 12, 2026. He will succeed Noel N. Tata, who is scheduled to relinquish the position a day earlier, marking a significant transition at the Tata Group’s air-conditioning and engineering business.

The appointments were approved at a board meeting held on November 6. Tata, who has served on Voltas’s board since 2003, will retire as chairman and director under the Tata Group’s superannuation policy. He will take on the designation of Chairman Emeritus from November 12.
D’Souza is already a member of the Voltas board and will assume the chairmanship alongside his existing responsibilities as managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Consumer Products.

D’Souza became the head of Tata Consumer Products in April 2020. Prior to that, he led Whirlpool India as managing director for close to five years, overseeing the company's business in India and neighbouring markets.

His professional experience also includes nearly 15 years at PepsiCo, where he held commercial and general management roles across India and several Asian markets, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia.
He began his career in 1993 at Hindustan Unilever, working in sales. Earlier, he had started out as a service engineer with Siemens.
D’Souza holds a bachelor’s degree in electronics and communications engineering from the University of Madras and a postgraduate management diploma from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta.
Voltas names successor to managing director
Voltas has also outlined a separate transition for its managing director’s office. C.P. Mukundan Menon, the company’s current managing director, will retire on May 24, 2027.

Jayant Balan, who currently leads Voltas’s room air-conditioner business, has been selected to succeed him from May 25, 2027. His appointment will be for a five-year term, subject to shareholder approval. Until then, Balan will serve as managing director designate.

In another board-level appointment, Voltas has named Venkatesalu Palaniswamy, former managing director of Trent, as an additional non-independent, non-executive director. His appointment will also take effect on November 12.

The leadership announcements coincide with an improvement in Voltas’s latest quarterly performance. The company reported a 53.5 per cent year-on-year increase in quarterly profit to Rs 526.4 million, while revenue grew 10.9 per cent to Rs 25.68 billion.
Its unitary cooling products business, which includes room air conditioners, recorded revenue growth of 29 per cent.
Tata’s departure from the Voltas chairmanship comes shortly after he retired as vice chairman and director of jewellery maker Titan Company on November 5.
